You hear a conversation between a GP and an office manager about staff
 burnout.
 What does the GP identify as a negative effect on the practice’s patients?
A. The quality of care they are receiving.
B. The amount of time they have to wait.
C. The level of stress they are feeling.

You hear a trainee doctor asking a senior doctor about a patient’s chest X-ray.

 The senior doctor points out the importance of…
A. The markings and tubular shadows in the upper lobes on the
 chest X-ray.
B. The prominence of the pulmonary arteries on the chest X-ray.
C. The repeated chest infections that the patient has had.

You hear part of a training about sports nutrition.
 Who is the audience for the training?
A. The training is for professional athletes training for competitive
 sports.
B. The training is for general practitioners involved in helping
 athletes recover from sports injuries.
C. The training is for dietitians who may be referred by a general
 practitioner.

You hear a morning briefing on a ward.
 The doctor explains that a head CT will help…
A. To eliminate another possible diagnosis.
B. To assess the neurological deficiencies.
C. To determine the next diagnostic step.

You hear part of a training on handovers between nurses.
 What does the doctor demonstrate with the example?
A. How to link two parts of the patient handover.
B. How to give all necessary information.
C. How to decide which type of information to include.

You hear a conversation between a GP and a neurologist.
 The GP has contacted the neurologist primarily because…
A. There was some information left out of the patient’s file.
B. She is very worried about the prognosis of the patient.
C. She was concerned that the notes contradict the patient’s
 symptoms.

The interviewee says it is important to talk about her profession in order
 to...
A. Make people aware of what the profession includes because it is
 a small profession.
B. Encourage future professionals in this small field of medicine.
C. Establish a clear career path in the profession for the next
 generation of dietitians.

According to the interviewee, what types of roles do dietitians now have?
A. They have maintained the same roles in healthcare that they have
 always had.
B. They have fluid and indeterminate roles in modern healthcare
 now.
C. They have added roles traditionally held by other healthcare
 professionals.

According to the interviewee, what big changes in health care have
 affected dietitians?
A. Efforts to reduce the cost of healthcare
B. Efforts to make healthcare more modern
C. Efforts to increase job satisfaction

Why does the interviewee discuss the case of a patient?
A. To demonstrate the increased complexity of dietitian’s cases
B. To demonstrate the potential of the profession of dietetics
C. To demonstrate the need for additional training for dietitians

What is the purpose of four pillars of practice?
A. To guide the career development of advanced practitioners
B. To help new dietitians in the field to start their career
C. To guide the profession of dietetics as practice changes

According to the interviewee, what is holding back the profession?
A. The lack of new professionals in the field
B. The lack of funding for the extended roles
C. The lack of funding for basic dietitian services

What is the main topic of the research described by the presenter?
A. The variety of challenges facing general practitioners
B. A particular challenge facing general practitioners
C. A challenge facing the future of general practitioners

According to the presenter, why is it a challenge for GPs to diagnose older
 adults with infection?
A. Because they often don’t go to their GP for diagnosis
B. Because they often don’t have this condition
C. Because they often display unusual symptoms

How did the research project gather data?
A. It invited GPs to a group session to talk about their work.
B. It invited GPs to individual sessions to talk about their work
C. It analysed previous comments by GPs about their work

According to the presenter, what is the role of medications in challenges
 leading to diagnostic uncertainty?
A. It can make it easier to diagnose infections in older patients.
B. It can make it more complicated to diagnose infections in older
 patients.
C. It has no measurable effect in diagnosing infections in older
 patients.

Why have GPs lost their ability to follow up with patients?
A. Because most GPs change practices frequently.
B. Because most GPs work less hours than before.
C. Because of the increased workload of GPs.

What limits the use of investigations to diagnose infection in older
 patients?
A. The amount of time that GPs have to wait for results.
B. The lack of available tests for this population of patients.
C. The pre-existing conditions of the older patients.
